summary: State-machine string-to-float parser (CRT strtod-style). Skips leading whitespace, then parses an optional sign, integer and fraction digit runs, and an optional decimal exponent, dispatching states through the jump table jpt_5962A8. Digit classification uses the char-type table off_5E69C8 (bit 4) or CharacterEncodingConvertViaLookupTableFallback when cbMultiByte exceeds 1; byte_5E6BD8 is the decimal separator. Collected digits fill a 25-entry buffer (cap 0x19) with overflow count v47; leading zeros and exponent combine into a base-10 exponent v23 (bounds +/-5200) adjusted by format scales a5/a6. sub_597621 packs the digit buffer into a 96-bit value across v34/v35/v36, and BitPackedDataDecodeViaLookupTable applies the exponent. The 96-bit result is written to the output (low word at a1+0, mid dword at a1+2, high dword at a1+6, sign-or-exponent word at a1+10) and a classification code v44 is returned: 4 for no digits parsed, 2 on overflow, 1 on underflow, else 0. The end-of-parse pointer is stored to *a2.

local_names.a1: output buffer for the packed 96-bit result
local_names.a2: output pointer receiving the end-of-parse input pointer
local_names.a3: working copy of the input string pointer
local_names.a5: format scale term added into the exponent when the integer flag v41 is clear
local_names.a6: format scale term subtracted from the exponent when the fraction flag v40 is clear
local_names.v8: parser state id dispatched through the jump table
local_names.v48: digit count into the collection buffer (cap 24)

operations.description: Skip leading whitespace (space 32, tab 9, newline 10, carriage return 13) until a non-whitespace byte is reached
State-machine parse loop over the input bytes driven by state v8; the dispatch reads the jump table jpt_5962A8
Sign handling: '+' clears the sign flag v39, '-' sets v39 to 0x8000 (negative bit)
Digit classification: char-type table off_5E69C8 bit 4 decides digit vs non-digit, or CharacterEncodingConvertViaLookupTableFallback when cbMultiByte exceeds 1
Collect integer digits into the 25-entry (0x19) buffer v32 through v46, incrementing the overflow count v47 once the cap is exceeded
Decimal separator: byte_5E6BD8 switches the parser from integer collection (state 3) to fraction collection (state 4)
Collect fraction digits, stripping leading zeros by decrementing v47; the digit count v48 caps at 24 with a rounding bump tracked in v33
Exponent handling: the exponent sign sets v43 to 1 or -1, and v42 accumulates the decimal exponent, capped at 5201
Combine digit count v47, sign-adjusted exponent v42, and format scales a5/a6 into the base-10 exponent v23, bounds-checked to +/-5200
sub_597621(v32, v48, v34) converts the collected digit buffer into a 96-bit packed value spanning v34/v35/v36
BitPackedDataDecodeViaLookupTable(v34, v23, a4) applies the base-10 exponent to the 96-bit value
Write the 96-bit result into the output: low word at a1+0, mid dword at a1+2, high dword at a1+6, and the sign-or-exponent word at a1+10
Result classification v44: 4 when no digits were parsed (v45 clear), 2 on overflow (v38), 1 on underflow (v37), else 0; *a2 stores the end-of-parse pointer
Called by EncodingLocaleDetectionFromParseResult, BufferFormatHelper and StringParseWithFormat
